name: msgspec for JSON/MessagePack hot paths
short_definition: msgspec is a zero-dependency high-performance serialization and validation library (JSON, MessagePack, YAML, TOML) built around msgspec.Struct and typed decode. Official benchmarks claim ~10–80× faster encode/decode+validate than alternatives for supported types, with Structs 5–60× faster than dataclasses/attrs for common ops. In the engineer stack it is a P2 opt-in for internal hot paths (queues, WebSocket fanout, bulk export, inter-service MessagePack) — not a greenfield replacement for Pydantic on FastAPI request/response models.
scope_in: When Pydantic v2 validation/serialization cost dominates CPU (measured)
Internal DTOs: workers, Redis streams, NATS/Kafka payloads, gRPC-adjacent JSON bridges
MessagePack binary envelopes between Python services
Bulk JSON encode/decode (export jobs, ML feature batches, log shippers)
msgspec.Struct schema design, ValidationError handling, convert() between types
Coexistence with Pydantic at HTTP edge vs msgspec on internal paths
scope_out: Default FastAPI body/query models (stay on Pydantic for OpenAPI, settings, DX)
UI or TypeScript schema generation (OpenAPI stays Pydantic-driven unless custom)
Full Litestar/Ravyn migration solely for msgspec

defaults.greenfield_http: Pydantic v2 BaseModel on FastAPI; do not introduce msgspec until a profiled hot path exists
defaults.hot_path: Define msgspec.Struct for internal messages; msgspec.json.encode/decode or msgspec.msgpack for binary; validate on decode with type=
defaults.boundary: HTTP edge = Pydantic; worker/queue/ws internal = msgspec optional
defaults.conversion: Map Struct ↔ Pydantic only at the boundary with explicit convert functions; avoid dual models on same public API
defaults.python: 3.12+ preferred; same as service runtime pin

use_when: py-spy/scalene shows encode/validate in top CPU for high-QPS or large-payload paths
Internal-only contracts (no need for FastAPI OpenAPI from those types)
MessagePack or multi-million object JSON pipelines
Shared message types across worker processes where dependency weight matters
do_not_use_when: CRUD API with DB-bound latency (server/JSON is not the bottleneck)
You need rich Pydantic features: custom validators, computed fields, settings, extensive JSON Schema
Team has no measured perf problem — premature dual-stack tax
Public OpenAPI must auto-generate from the same models without extra tooling

alternatives.pydantic_v2: Default for FastAPI + settings + agent DX
alternatives.orjson: Fast JSON bytes only; no schema validation
alternatives.rust_boundary: If hot path is multi-GB/s or correctness-critical parsers, hand off to Rust/serde

do: Profile before adopting; record baseline p50/p99 and CPU share
Validate untrusted bytes on decode: msgspec.json.decode(data, type=MyStruct)
Prefer Struct for schemas; use plain encode for trusted internal dicts only when intentional
Catch msgspec.ValidationError at boundaries; map to domain errors
Pin msgspec in uv.lock; keep one version monorepo-wide
Document which endpoints/workers use msgspec vs Pydantic
dont: Don't assume Struct constructor validates types (constructor does not; decode does)
Don't replace all Pydantic models wholesale in a FastAPI app without OpenAPI plan
Don't decode untrusted input without type=
Don't mix silent orjson + msgspec + pydantic paths without ownership
Don't invent dual public schemas that drift

failure_modes: Assuming Point(x=1, y='oops') raises — Struct init does not type-check; only decode validates
Silent schema drift between producer Struct and consumer Struct (no shared package)
Using msgspec types in FastAPI path params expecting Pydantic/OpenAPI magic
Large nested dict fields re-introduce Python object cost (Struct only helps typed shape)
Wrong protocol (JSON vs msgpack) across services → opaque decode failures
ValidationError not mapped → 500s or worker crash loops on poison messages
anti_patterns: Agent generates msgspec for every FastAPI model by default
Dual BaseModel and Struct for same public DTO without conversion tests
decode without type= on untrusted network input
Catching Exception and ignoring ValidationError details
Pulling msgspec just for yaml/toml config when pydantic-settings is standard

versions_as_of.note: Pins labeled as_of research date; re-resolve with uv lock before ship

config_snippets.uv_add: uv add msgspec  # after profiling gate, not greenfield default
config_snippets.ruff: # no special ruff plugin; treat Struct like dataclass for imports

deprecation_watch: Do not start greenfield APIs on marshmallow / pydantic v1 for perf — use Pydantic v2 first, msgspec only if still hot
Avoid orjson as sole validator (no schema)
Avoid custom C extensions for JSON without need once msgspec covers the path
ts_boundary: msgspec types are not auto-exported to TS. Public contracts stay OpenAPI from FastAPI/Pydantic or hand-written JSON Schema. Internal msgspec payloads should not be consumed by Next BFF unless you publish a stable schema and version it. Prefer BFF talking HTTP JSON validated by Pydantic; use msgspec only behind Python workers.
rust_boundary: If encode/decode remains CPU-bound after msgspec (multi-GB streams, custom binary protocols, strict latency SLOs), move the hot parser/serializer to Rust (serde_json / rmp-serde) and expose via PyO3 or a small Axum sidecar. msgspec is the last Python-native stop before Rust.
supabase_boundary: Do not replace PostgREST/Supabase client models with msgspec. Use msgspec for internal job payloads that reference row IDs; keep DB row validation at SQLAlchemy/Pydantic or RLS layer. Never put service-role keys in Struct defaults.
boundary_contracts: Version internal MessagePack/JSON envelopes (e.g. envelope.v + schema_id)
OpenAPI remains Pydantic-generated for external clients
Env secrets via pydantic-settings, not msgspec

decision_matrix_row.python: msgspec.Struct + json/msgpack after profiling; Pydantic at HTTP edge
decision_matrix_row.ts: Zod/valibot on BFF/edge only; do not reimplement msgspec in TS
decision_matrix_row.rust: When throughput/latency exceeds Python+msgspec budget or protocol is custom binary

threats: Untrusted decode without type= → type confusion / unexpected structures
Over-permissive dict[str, Any] fields smuggle attacker-controlled graphs into workers
Schema confusion attacks if multiple message types share a bus without discriminators
DoS via huge JSON documents if no size limits at proxy/app
mitigations: Always decode(data, type=Struct) for untrusted input
Enforce max body size at reverse proxy and ASGI layer
Use tagged unions / explicit type field for multi-message channels
frozen=True Structs for immutability after decode

must_generate: Comment or module docstring stating why msgspec (measured hot path)
must_not_generate: msgspec as default for all FastAPI models
Struct without tests for invalid payloads
Silent fallthrough from ValidationError to generic 500 without logging

tests_required: Invalid payload matrix (wrong types, missing fields, extra fields policy)
Boundary convert tests if dual Pydantic/msgspec models exist
Optional: pytest-benchmark guard on critical path
ci_gates: ruff + basedpyright on modules importing msgspec
uv lock includes msgspec only if declared dependency

positive: msgspec used in workers/queues with type= decode
Profile evidence or comment justifying hot-path use
negative: msgspec.Struct as only API model layer with no OpenAPI story
json.loads + manual dict without schema on same hot path
decode without type= on network/queue input
Both orjson and msgspec without documented split

skill_module_bullets: Default HTTP validation: Pydantic v2; msgspec is P2 hot-path only after profiling
msgspec.Struct validates on decode, not on constructor — always type= for untrusted bytes
Prefer msgspec for internal JSON/MessagePack buses and bulk jobs; keep OpenAPI on Pydantic
Pin msgspec as_of 2026-07-13: 0.21.x; do not dual-stack casually
If msgspec still not enough → Rust serde boundary

Add scan rule: msgspec in api/routes without justification → warn
Optional example worker using msgspec.msgpack in skill samples
checklist: Structs frozen where appropriate; decode uses type=
conflicts_noted: Community blog claims vary widely (3×–15× vs Pydantic v2); official msgspec docs state ~10–80× for supported types vs alternatives and ~12× vs Pydantic v2 on their validation benchmark — treat exact multiples as workload-dependent
Some teams advocate msgspec as default DTO layer (Litestar); FastAPI ecosystem remains Pydantic-first — engineer follows FastAPI default
